title: Capacity forecast sprintboard — annotated summary
content:
Summary

This note is an annotated readout from the sprintboard session on capacity forecasting (week of 2028-02-13 → 2028-02-19). The goal: reconcile short-term demand surges (customer trials + marketing promotion) with our multi-region soft-slot budget and pre-warm strategy without increasing committed reserved spend. This is a working document — decisions are tentative and flagged as ACTION items.

Top-level conclusions
- Expected 28–42% uplift in token serving demand across US-West and EU-Central in the next 4 weeks (see demand model v2 in linked Confluence). Uplift concentrated in mid-late business hours PST/CEST.
- Shortfall risk: our current soft-slot headroom in US-West is ~9% under idealized routing assumptions; EU-Central has ~12% headroom but higher tail-latency variance during priming windows.
- Immediate mitigation that the sprintboard greenlit: apply targeted soft-slot rebalancing from APAC edge pools → US-West for next 3 business days and enable aggressive prefix cache warmers for the top 25 customer prefixes.

Data highlights and signals reviewed
- Traffic signal: daily 00:00–04:00 PST batch job spikes now shifted +2 hours (users pushing scheduled tasks later). Demand model v2 captures this by weight shifting the peak; see time-series snapshot.
- Queueing telemetry: percentile queue wait (p99.9) on GPU inference queues spiked by 210ms for 8-minute windows on 2028-02-15 coincident with auto-scaler reconciling burst slots.
- Cold-starts: KV cache miss ratio rose to 17% for long chats (>6k tokens) during regional canary on 2028-02-17.
- Cost signal: spot preemption rates have a clustered correlation with provider maintenance windows in APAC, increasing evictions by ~3.5% on average in local nights.

Annotated sprintboard (key lanes)
1) Soft-slot budget lane (owner: Diego Ramos)
- Observation: soft-slot budget is currently allocated based on monthly moving-average demand per tenant. This underweights short-lived new customers (trial accounts) causing temporary overflows.
- Proposed change: introduce a sliding short-term multiplier (72-hour) for tenants with >2× baseline burst in that window.
- Risk/Tradeoff: could oscillate if multiple tenants spike simultaneously; mitigate via dampening factor and cap at +30% per-tenant.
- ACTION: Diego to prototype multiplier and run 48-hour sim against last 6 months of traces. Jira JIRA-INFRA-7598 assigned.

2) Regional pre-warm & cache lane (owner: Priya Nambiar)
- Observation: prefix cache warmers have lowered per-token latency for top-10 customer prefixes but heat coverage is patchy outside the top decile.
- Experiment: roll out a probabilistic warmer that uses time-of-day heuristics and a lightweight demand predictor (v2) to prefetch the top-25 prefixes in US-West & EU-Central. Warmers will warm only for prefixes with expected hit-rate > 18% to avoid waste.
- ACTION: Priya + data-science to run a 72-hour A/B in US-West window 14:00–21:00 PST. Monitoring dashboard: /dashboards/prefetch-warmers.

3) Spot/eviction resilience lane (owner: Eun-Ji Park)
- Observation: APAC edge preemptions cluster with provider maintenance. Our current fallback path to regional spare capacity adds latency >150ms in several cases.
- Short-term mitigation: reserve a tiny high-QOS pool (soft-reserve) in APAC equal to 2% of regional capacity; only used when predicted eviction risk > 4%.
- ACTION: Eun-Ji to coordinate with cloud ops to carve soft-reserve and update failover policy (runbook PR).

4) Autoscaler and packer tuning lane (owner: Liam Chen)
- Observation: autoscaler step-downs are too aggressive during ephemeral drops; cold nodes cause additional priming lag.
- Change: lengthen scale-down cooldown from 3m → 9m for GPU-backed scaling groups handling chat workloads. Add hysteresis based on rolling median CPU/GPU utilization.
- ACTION: Liam to stage rollout in canary region (us-west2-c) this week.

Operational runbook deltas (proposed, not yet merged)
- New priority: dynamic soft-slot rebalancer (temporal) — small controller that shifts soft-slot budgets between regions per a heartbeat (every 15m). It will respect reserve floor and a max-transfer-per-cycle to prevent oscillation.
- New alert: p99.95 queue-weighted wait > 350ms for >5min -> auto-trigger warmers and increase soft-slot cap by +5% (if available).
- Fallback: if rebalancer cannot find spare soft-slots for 30m, traffic should route to compatible quantized model variant with a lower footprint (model fallback policy '#alpha-quant').

Decision log (explicit approvals)
- APPROVED (triage): short-term soft-slot rebalancer experiment (3-day run) — agreed 2028-02-20 by on-call and infra leads.
- APPROVED: increase scale-down cooldown for GPU scaling groups in chat path (canary region first).

Open questions / risks
- How aggressively do we want to budget warmers while balancing token cost? Warmers do add tokens (and therefore cost) — proposed guard: cap warmers to 0.7% of baseline daily tokens for each region.
- Can model fallback maintain QoE for top-tier customers? Need small sample evaluation against our regression suite.
- Coordination risk: APAC soft-reserve carve may impact partner workloads; Eun-Ji to run partner impact simulation.

Action items (owner, ETA)
- Diego: prototype sliding short-term multiplier + 48h sim (ETA 2028-02-23).
- Priya: launch probabilistic prefix-warmer A/B in US-West, 72h (ETA start 2028-02-21).
- Eun-Ji: carve APAC 2% soft-reserve + update runbook PR (ETA 2028-02-22).
- Liam: canary rollout of scale-down cooldown increase in us-west2-c (ETA 2028-02-21).
- Maya (owner of this note): collect A/B metrics and host follow-up sync on 2028-02-24 10:30 PST.

Appendix: quick numbers snapshot (baseline vs projected peak)
- US-West baseline token/s: 185k. Projected 4-week peak token/s (90th): 252k (+36%).
- EU-Central baseline token/s: 92k. Projected 4-week peak token/s (90th): 126k (+37%).
- APAC baseline token/s: 47k. Projected shift: neutral overall, but night-time eviction risk uptick +3.5%.

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally concise: please comment inline in Confluence CAPACITY-BOARD-2028 if you want changes to the runbook text. For immediate ops changes, comment on JIRA-INFRA-7598.

Meeting attendees (sprintboard): Maya Langley, Diego Ramos, Priya Nambiar, Eun-Ji Park, Liam Chen, Nico Alvarez (SRE advisor), Anna Schultz (customer-ops).

Raw traces & dashboards referenced (for reviewers)
- /dashboards/capacity/sprintboard-v2 (time-series snapshots)
- /dashboards/prefetch-warmers (A/B monitoring)

End of note.
